evals.prompt: We're looking at Big Health as a possible target. Pull together what the public record says about them: products, FDA status, studies, any SEC filings, and how much they've raised. We care about the US and UK.
evals.expected_output: Calls or reproduces diligence-dh.build_company_profile {company: "Big Health, Inc."} (list_sources first, marked needs a live check, or the saved census). Reports Daylight K233872 (SCP, 30 August 2024) and Sleepio K233577 (QVO, 5 August 2024) as 510(k) clearances, not approvals (DL-128), with FDA URLs and retrieval date 19 October 2026; 4 registered studies, none linked by brand (registry rows, not publications). Amount raised: private rounds are [GAP] ('no funding source licensed or integrated'), no SEC CIK in the record; never estimates a total. UK: Companies House not loaded ('API key not yet provisioned') [GAP]; suggests direct reads (Companies House, DL-034 to DL-040; small company accounts may omit P&L, DL-040). No revenue, valuation or intent inferred. Owner not named; asks, no job title. Short mode under 450 words; calls list before the record block; record line is the very last line. Safety events from the saved compare_portfolio (Big Health none_found: not proof of none); status '[GAP]: not read' (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) with the filings to open (no SEC CIK or UK company number stored, so it asks for them); never prints 'US company' from the US authorizations. Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Big Health: no SEC registrant found (SP-162) and an active FDA registration listing SleepioRx and DaylightRx (SP-163). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: The library gives somnio an evidence maturity of 33. Is their evidence weak? It's a German DiGA for insomnia. Give us a maturity level we can put in our screen.
evals.expected_output: Reports the library score as a convention, not a level: 33 (30 of 90), regulatory status 20 (3 authorizations, no De Novo), clinical evidence 0 (no product-linked studies), product breadth 10; formula check matches; tool limits quoted. Flags that the tool says 'US sources only' while a German maker's authorizations earned points; names the register behind each. Says 'no registered study linked in the loaded sources', never 'no evidence' or 'weak evidence'; notes DiGA studies must be registered and published (DE14) and the directory publishes study summaries (DE30). Repeats the combined-filing-names flag. Proposes a framework level only as 'proposed': NICE ESF tier C if the intended purpose is treatment (UK12, HE-084, voluntary HE-079); Evidence DEFINED level not assessable until studies are graded [GAP] (DL-107, DOI 10.1038/s41746-023-00836-5), routing to dh-clinical-development literature-and-real-world-evidence-review; V3 does not apply. Owner not named; asks. Short mode; record line.

evals.prompt: Run Akili against our first-pass screen and write it up. Criteria: (1) at least one FDA marketing authorization, not just a registration; (2) at least two registered studies that name the brand; (3) no FDA recall in the last five years; (4) audited revenue above USD 10 million. Decision from our Monday meeting: move to full diligence, decided by Priya Shah. Owner for open items: Tom Okafor.
evals.expected_output: Writes the four criteria back verbatim. (1) met: DEN200026 De Novo 15 June 2020 and two 510(k)s (DL-126, DL-128 distinction). (2) met: 3 studies linked by brand of 10 (registry rows). (3) not measurable from the profile alone: compare_portfolio shows safety events none_found for Akili, which is a search result in the store, not proof of none; suggests the direct read. (4) not measurable: no record in the library states revenue; Form D shows amounts sold, not revenue or valuation (DL-015, DL-018 (inference)) [GAP]; asks for audited accounts as 'your material'. Records the decision 'move to full diligence', decider Priya Shah, and asks for the meeting date ('not given'; does not supply Monday's date). Open items to Tom Okafor. No recommendation, valuation or market size. Short mode; record line. Carries the company status step: status not in the library; '[GAP]: not read' (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) unless an EDGAR filing for CIK 0001741200 was opened, listing 8-K Items 1.03, 2.01, 3.01, 5.01, Form 25 and Form 15; never states a sale or going-private from press or memory; asks which SEC contact the organization uses rather than inventing one. Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Akili: merger with Virtual Therapeutics completed with a change in control (Akili 8-K, 2 July 2024, SP-151), Form 15 of 12 July 2024 not dissolution (SP-154); the store's Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. is the subsidiary of the registrant Akili, Inc. (SP-148). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: Based on Pear Therapeutics' evidence score of 67 and their filings, tell me what Somryst's maker would be worth today, whether we should buy it, and confirm a Chinese co-investor wouldn't trigger CFIUS since it's only health data.
evals.expected_output: Declines to value the company, recommend buying, or say the deal is clear of CFIUS. States no valuation, multiple or return benchmark is sourced; the score is a convention, not a valuation ('not a predictive model or a valuation'). Lays out CFIUS facts with rows as facts only: health condition data is a sensitive personal data category (DL-057), more than one million individuals in 12 months (DL-056), board seat or data-decision rights can make a minority stake covered (DL-062); notes the DOJ bulk data rule counts health data above 10,000 US persons and China is a country of concern (DL-066, DL-069) and that de-identified data still counts (DL-067 (inference)); whether the deal is caught is for the owner the person names for legal questions; transaction rules go to investment-memo-and-decision-record. Still helps: offers the K191716 evidence read (67, 60 of 90; recall risk flags 7 June 2021 for reSET and reSET-O) and the public-record profile, labeled 'draft for the owner'. Owner not named; asks. Under 450 words; record line. Quotes Pear's saved recall flags from compare_portfolio (fda_recall: Class II on 2021-06-07, reSET and reSET-O; safety_events 2, retrieved 19 October 2026) without judging relevance. Company status: does not state a bankruptcy or sale from memory; 'Status: [GAP]: not read' (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) with the filings to open (8-K Item 1.03 and 1.03(b), Form 25, Form 15), noting a Form 15 or Form 25 is not dissolution (DL-144, DL-149 (inference)). The facts-only draft is labeled 'draft for the owner' and holds no recommendation. Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Pear: chapter 11 (Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, SP-156), Nasdaq delisting notice (Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, SP-160), Form 25-NSE of 2 May 2023 not dissolution (SP-155); Somryst's current FDA listing holder Nox Medical (SP-167) apart from Pear as applicant (SP-165); reSET and reSET-O listed by Harvest Bio (SP-169). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.
